attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Sharma, MD
Department: Obstetrics & Gynecology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Dysuria, increased urinary frequency, and yellow vaginal discharge for 5 days

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
She presents to the clinic with a 5-day history of dysuria, increased urinary frequency, and a yellow vaginal discharge. Her last menstrual period was 3 weeks ago, and she denies any recent changes in her menstrual cycle.

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal grandmother with breast cancer (age 65)
- Father with hypertension
- Mother with hypothyroidism

SOCIAL HISTORY:
She reports having multiple sexual partners over the past 6 months and inconsistently using condoms.

VITAL SIGNS:
37.8°C (100°F)

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, she has a temperature of 37.8°C (100°F), and a pelvic exam reveals cervical motion tenderness and a purulent cervical discharge.

LABORATORY DATA:
Urine nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) is positive for Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Additional laboratory tests are as follows:

- HIV 1/2 antigen/antibody: Negative
- Rapid plasma reagin (RPR): Non-reactive
- Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg): Negative
- Urine pregnancy test: Negative

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-01-15
Provider: Dr. Emily Carter, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Fever, diffuse lower abdominal pain, and vaginal discharge for 2 days

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
Patient returns with fever, diffuse lower abdominal pain, and vaginal discharge after prior Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection and suspected pelvic inflammatory disease. Last menstrual period was 3 weeks ago, and she denies any possibility of pregnancy.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection (Gonococcal cervicitis) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Pelvic inflammatory disease (suspected) (diagnosed 2020-04-15)

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal grandmother with breast cancer (age 65)
- Father with hypertension
- Mother with hypothyroidism

SOCIAL HISTORY:
She reports multiple sexual partners and inconsistent condom use.

VITAL SIGNS:
On examination, her temperature is 39.2°C (102.5°F), heart rate is 110/min, and blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Pelvic examination reveals cervical motion tenderness, bilateral adnexal tenderness, and a mucopurulent cervical discharge.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory tests are as follows:

- White blood cell count: 15,000/mm³
- Neutrophils: 80%
- Hemoglobin: 12.5 g/dL
- Urine pregnancy test: Negative
- Nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) for Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae: Pending

Department: Obstetrics & Gynecology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Painful urination and increased urinary frequency for 5 days following unprotected intercourse with a new partner 2 weeks ago

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to the clinic three months after a prior Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection and presents with a 5-day history of painful urination and increased urinary frequency. She denies vaginal discharge or bleeding, but reports having unprotected sexual intercourse with a new partner 2 weeks ago.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection (Gonococcal cervicitis) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

MEDICATIONS:
She takes no medications.

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal grandmother with breast cancer (age 65)
- Father with hypertension
- Mother with hypothyroidism

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional social use, 2-3 drinks per month. Occupation: University student, part-time retail associate.

VITAL SIGNS:
On physical examination, her vital signs are within normal limits

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Abdominal examination reveals no tenderness. Pelvic examination is notable for cervical motion tenderness.

LABORATORY DATA:
Urinalysis shows:
- Leukocyte esterase: Positive
- Nitrites: Negative
- WBC: 10-20/hpf
- RBC: 0-2/hpf
- No bacteria or yeast cells seen
